evidence_quotes.section1_quid_pro_quo: Calvin mentions availability and moving on Nov 1st but never frames the 10-15 min call length or 'quote you can depend on' promise, and never waits for a yes before diving into details.
evidence_quotes.discovery_basics: Moving date (Nov 1st) and route (same street, few houses up) mentioned; home size comes up late as 'two bedroom' initially then corrected to 4-bedroom. Name (Erica) obtained. Some basics present but scattered and reactive.
evidence_quotes.their_agenda: Never asked. Calvin immediately responds to Erica's unsolicited price question ('what do you guys charge') without first establishing her concerns and priorities.
evidence_quotes.estimate_anchor: Calvin provides hourly rate ($96/hour per guy, 2.5-hour minimum, billing in 15-minute increments) and later gives a range anchor: 'typically four guys... $384 hourly rate... full day... more like $23,000 is pretty standard for a big home like this.' The anchor is present but arrived at very late and only after budget conflict arose.
evidence_quotes.pricing_framing: Calvin clearly explains all-inclusive rate (no taxes, trip fees, credit card fees; pads, wrap, disassembly, reassembly, insurance included), the 2.5-hour minimum, and 15-minute increment billing. This is comprehensive fee transparency and commitment framing. However, 'not a guess' language is not present.
evidence_quotes.feels_fair_then_silence: Never asked. Call ends with customer saying 'let me talk to my husband' — no explicit 'Does that feel fair?' ask from Calvin, and no real pause held.
evidence_quotes.two_promises: On-Time Guarantee never mentioned. No Worries Damage Coverage never mentioned. Entire Section 5 omitted.
evidence_quotes.final_concerns_check: Never asked. Call ends abruptly after Erica says she'll discuss with husband.
evidence_quotes.explicit_ask: Never asked. Calvin never says 'Would you like our help with your move?' or any equivalent. Call trails off as a price-check inquiry.
evidence_quotes.section1_walkthrough_branch: Property is 2,700 sq ft (well over 1,800), but the walkthrough offer is never made. However, this is a reactive price-check call driven entirely by the customer's budget objection; Calvin does not intentionally skip the walkthrough — the call structure itself never reaches that pivot point because discovery and the quid pro quo framing were missing.

top_strength: Calvin clearly articulated all-inclusive pricing and fee transparency ($96/hour, 2.5-hour minimum, 15-minute billing, no hidden fees) in a way the customer understood, and he did the math to show why her $500 budget was unrealistic for her scope.
coaching_note: Open with the quid pro quo framing (10-15 min call, dependable quote, get a yes) before responding to price questions; this would have anchored the call and allowed proper discovery, including the walkthrough offer for this 2,700 sq ft home, instead of falling into a budget-objection spiral.
